sections.h2: Who do I call about a Stephenson County tax bill?
sections.html:
Stephenson County splits the work between three desks in Freeport. The Treasurer and Collector sends and takes payment on bills, at the Stewart Centre, 50 West Douglas Street, Suite 503 (fifth floor), 815-235-8264, with a counter that opens at 8:30 in the morning and closes at 4:30 on weekdays The treasurer's page states plainly that the office does not set assessed values, exemptions or bill amounts.

  • Assessment questions, exemptions, mapping, address clarifications and assessment complaints: the Assessor's office, 815-235-8260.
  • Redemption amounts after a tax sale: the County Clerk, 815-235-8289.
  • Filing a complaint: the clerk of the Board of Review, 50 West Douglas Street, Suite 502.

One local wrinkle matters for owners inside the city. Freeport Township assesses its own parcels, and their numbers begin with 18. The county assessor handles the other 17 townships. The Freeport Township Assessor is at 524 W. Stephenson St., Suite 214, 815-232-6131.

sections.h2: How do Stephenson County's size and housing mix affect a sale?
sections.html:
Freeport anchors Stephenson County, a northwestern Illinois county. It was formed in 1837 from land that had belonged to Jo Daviess and Winnebago counties, and the first settler, in 1832, founded Waddams Grove. Today it covers 565 square miles and touches the Wisconsin line at Green and Lafayette counties.

Census figures show 44,630 residents in 2020 and an estimated 43,220 for 2025. Of the county's 21,369 housing units, 10.2 percent were vacant, and among occupied homes 70.4 percent were owner-occupied. The median age is 45.9. Roughly 54 percent of residents are classed as urban and 46 percent as rural.

January days in Freeport average a high of 25 and a low of 9 degrees, and July highs reach about 82. Cold winters put furnace age and roof condition high on a buyer's list. The county's public high schools are Freeport, Lena-Winslow, Dakota, Pearl City and Orangeville, with Aquin Catholic as the private option.

sections.h2: What dates did Stephenson County set for 2026 payments?
sections.html:
The 2026 bill covered tax year 2025. Its first half was due Friday, June 26, the second half Friday, September 4, and the last day to pay real estate taxes was Monday, November 9. One bill goes out in May for both halves, and both can be paid together by the first date.

Stephenson County Treasurer calendar for the 2026 bill
DateWhat it marks
May 26, 2026Online lookup and payment opened
June 26, 2026First installment due
September 4, 2026Second installment due
November 9, 2026Last day to pay real estate taxes

Per the county's FAQ, a mailed installment is on time when the post office postmarks it by midnight of the due date. A postage meter stamp does not count, and the county urges mailers to leave margin. The last day before the tax sale works differently: payments must be received, not just postmarked, by the end of that business day. Partial payments are returned, because Illinois law does not allow the collector to accept them.

sections.h2: Where can I pay my Stephenson County tax bill?
sections.html:
Five routes are open. Every route needs the barcoded coupon, original or reprint, and banks ask for it too.

  • By mail to Stephenson County Collector, 50 W. Douglas St., Suite 503, Freeport, IL 61032.
  • In the payment dropbox just inside the Stewart Centre lobby. Cash does not go in the box.
  • In person at the treasurer's office on the fifth floor.
  • At most banks in the county. Fifth Third Bank and credit unions cannot take them.
  • Online through the county portal or your bank's bill pay. E-check carries a flat $2.95 fee that covers up to 99 payments, and none of the fees go to the county.

A lost bill can be printed free from the portal. An exact duplicate costs $1.00 per parcel for an owner and $5.00 for anyone else, and veterans pay no duplicate fee. A bill that never arrives still carries the tax and the penalty. If your mailing address is wrong, call the Assessor's office at 815-235-8260, which needs a signature on file to change it.

sections.h2: How is a Stephenson County bill calculated?
sections.html:
A bill is a taxable value times a rate. Assessors value each parcel as of January 1 and target one-third of fair market value, and a past assessment publication reported a median level of 33.33 percent. Credits and exemptions come off the assessed figure.

The rate depends on where the parcel sits. The county has 104 tax districts, and each parcel lies in its own mix of school, township, road, fire, park, library and county bodies. The county clerk's extension division divides each body's levy by its tax base. The county's page lists these exemptions, among others:

  • Owner Occupied Exemption.
  • Senior Citizen Homestead Exemption and Senior Citizen Freeze.
  • Homestead Improvement Exemption.
  • Disabled Veteran Exemption.

More than 26,000 bills go out each year. The county stresses that property is taxed, not people, and that each bill rests on the prior year's assessment for a full calendar year.

sections.h2: What is the process to dispute a Stephenson County assessment?
sections.html:
Talk to the township assessor or the chief county assessment office first. If that does not settle it, a written complaint must reach the Board of Review no later than 30 calendar days after your township's change list is published (35 ILCS 200/16-55). Once that date passes, the board cannot take complaints for the township.

Forms and instructions come from the assessment office at 815-235-8260, in person or online, and the completed form goes to the clerk of the Board of Review. A complaint mailed through the post office counts as filed on its postmark date. The county's own notices say the board is barred by law from accepting late ones.

A taxpayer who disagrees with the board has 30 days from written notice of its decision to petition the state Property Tax Appeal Board, or may sue in circuit court (35 ILCS 200/16-160). Only value is on the table. Rates and bill totals are set by other bodies.

sections.h2: What happens if Stephenson County taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
After each due date, a penalty of one and a half percent accrues every month, and it is not prorated. Section 21-15 of the Property Tax Code uses that rate for counties below 3,000,000 people.

In October, certified letters go to owners of unpaid parcels, and a notice runs in the Village Voices. The unpaid taxes are offered at a November tax sale. The sale auctions the tax, not the house, and a buyer who wins takes a lien at the interest rate bid. Afterward the delinquent records move to the County Clerk, 815-235-8289, who quotes redemption amounts.

The treasurer's FAQ says a home is at risk only if nothing clears the lien in 30 months. For certificates issued since the start of 2024, 35 ILCS 200/21-350 allows redemption for 3 years after the sale in most cases, so ask the clerk which period covers your parcel.

sections.h2: Who owes the tax when a Stephenson County house sells?
sections.html:
The county's FAQ says a split between buyer and seller is usually settled at closing and set out in the contract. Until a bill is paid, the present owner answers for the whole amount. A parcel with a balance can still change hands, since the unpaid tax is deducted from what the seller receives.

Before you list, take these steps:

  • Print the parcel's history from the county portal, which goes back to the 2000 tax year for most parcels.
  • Call the treasurer for the exact penalty on a late installment. The schedule is also printed on each coupon.
  • Check with your mortgage company whether it pays from escrow. If it does, a lender at fault for a late payment bears the penalty.
  • Confirm with the Assessor that exemptions on the parcel are current.

A Stephenson County house in rough shape can sell as is for cash, with the tax due paid at the table.

faqs.q: What was the final payment date for the 2026 Stephenson County bill?
faqs.a: Monday, November 9. The two halves had been due June 26 and September 4, with a penalty of one and a half percent a month after each.

faqs.q: Which office decides how much my Stephenson County bill is?
faqs.a: None alone. Assessors set values, taxing bodies set levies, and the county clerk extends rates. The Treasurer collects and cannot alter values, exemptions or amounts.

faqs.q: Does Stephenson County take a partial payment on an installment?
faqs.a: No. The two equal installments fall in June and September, and Illinois law bars the collector from accepting less than a full installment. A partial check is mailed back.

faqs.q: Is the county assessor responsible for Freeport parcels?
faqs.a: No. Freeport Township assesses its own parcels, which carry numbers starting with 18, while the county office covers the other 17 townships. Call the township office at 815-232-6131.

faqs.q: What is the deadline for a Stephenson County assessment complaint?
faqs.a: Thirty calendar days after your township's change list is published. The Board of Review cannot take a late complaint, and the state appeal needs a board decision first.
